data.description:
## Description

**What**: Add per-tier attempt counters (ceiling 5), global ceiling 15, cross-tier regression counter reset, budget-pressure context injection at attempt 4, CANNOT_PROCEED detection, /dso:oscillation-check integration, state file persistence of all remediation fields, full escalation JSON payload with all 7 stop_reason enum values, and exit code 2 for remediation exhaustion.

**Why**: Satisfies SC3 and completes SC4 — bounds the remediation loop to prevent runaway retries and provides a structured escalation output for human triage when automation cannot proceed.

**Scope**:
- IN: Per-tier attempt counters (ceiling 5); global ceiling 15 total attempts across all tiers; cross-tier regression reset (regressed tier counter → 0, global ceiling not reset); budget-pressure injection at attempt 4 of any tier ("This is attempt 4 of 5 — if you cannot resolve this finding, return ESCALATE with a clear explanation"); CANNOT_PROCEED detection from sub-agent ESCALATION_REASON; /dso:oscillation-check dispatch when same files targeted on attempt 2+; state file fields (remediation_attempts_per_tier, remediation_attempts_global, remediation_phase) persisted to /tmp/merge-to-main-state-<branch>.json; full escalation JSON payload (tiers_attempted, attempts_per_tier, remaining_findings, stop_reason, suggested_next_step) with all 7 stop_reason values (TIER_CEILING|GLOBAL_CEILING|CANNOT_PROCEED|OSCILLATION|THROTTLE_PAUSE|CONFLICT_RESOLUTION_FAILED|ARTIFACT_MISSING); exit code 2 (remediation exhaustion) vs exit code 1 (pre-remediation failure)
- OUT: New normalizer tier logic (→S2); conflict resolution dispatch logic (→S3)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, each tier maintains an independent attempt counter with ceiling 5; a global counter bounds total attempts at 15; a cross-tier regression (e.g., Tier 1 fix breaks Tier 2) resets the affected tier's counter to 0 without exceeding the global ceiling
  ← Satisfies: "SC3: Each tier maintains an independent attempt counter (ceiling: 5 per tier). A cross-tier regression resets the regressed tier's counter to 0. A global ceiling of 15 total attempts prevents infinite loops"
- When this story is complete, the escalation JSON payload (written to stdout) contains all 7 stop_reason values and the script exits with code 2 on remediation exhaustion vs code 1 on pre-remediation failure
  ← Satisfies: "SC4: On exhaustion of any tier's ceiling, global ceiling, CANNOT_PROCEED, or oscillation detection, the loop exits with a structured JSON escalation payload"
- When this story is complete, remediation_attempts_per_tier, remediation_attempts_global, and remediation_phase are all persisted in the merge-to-main state file, enabling --resume to continue after SIGURG interruption
  ← Satisfies: "SC3: All counters and phase state persist in the merge-to-main state file for SIGURG resume safety"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for counter reset logic, budget-pressure injection, and oscillation-check integration

## Considerations

- [Reliability] State file writes must be atomic (write to temp file, then rename) to prevent corruption if SIGURG interrupts mid-write
- [Consumer Impact] merge-to-main-pr.sh currently exits 1 on any failure; introducing exit 2 changes the exit-code contract. Audit merge-to-main.sh dispatcher, sprint SKILL.md, COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md, and any CI/wrapper scripts that branch on exit code to ensure exit 2 is handled (not collapsed to a generic non-zero failure that discards the escalation JSON)
- [Testing] Counter reset logic (cross-tier regression) needs isolated unit tests that don't require a full CI cycle
- THROTTLE_PAUSE stop_reason is emitted when usage-aware throttling returns MAX_AGENTS: 0; remediation state is preserved for manual retry

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As an agent operator, the remediation loop bounds retries, persists state across interruptions, and emits structured escalation
